problems:
The verdict holds, so refuted=false: as a GT oracle the three together give more than +0.01; nothing realistic gets close; R8 is unreachable. But the headline +0.021 is oversold, and so are several supporting claims. Checks: scratchpad/combo/v1_check.py -> v1_check_out.json, v1_boot.py; notes in v_joint_oracle_1.notes.md.
1. THE LINK THE USER ASKED ABOUT IS NOT THE LINK IN THE HEADLINE. The user added up round-11 numbers, so "links <= +0.003" means end->free-start linking. That naive sum is already 0.0063+0.0054+0.003 = 0.0147. Measured like for like (FP + ATT_g + L_remove_attach_noswap, same order LINK->ATT->FP): the joint is +0.01428 (44b6 +0.00860, 6bba +0.01458; div 32/0/67). The singles sum to 0.01276. The honest answer to the user's question is therefore +0.014, not +0.021. About +0.006 of the +0.021 comes from the 129 swaps. On 44b6 the like-for-like joint (+0.0086) is below the +0.012 bar.
2. THE SWAP EXPLANATION IS WRONG. The conclusion calls it fast motion: the solver gave v to a close unannotated neighbour while u made a "7 um true move". Measured against GT positions (129 swaps): the GT displacement |a->b| has median 2.19 um (56% under 3 um, only 29% at 5 um or more). |u-a| is 2.0 um, but v sits a median 4.61 um from b (71% over 3.5 um). The nearest other predicted node to b is 8.4 um away. So b has no good detection at t+1. v is w's near-stationary continuation (|wv| 1.8 um), and the Hungarian match takes it only loosely, inside the 7 um radius. The 7 um u->v gap is mostly match slack, not motion. The swap ceiling is a missing-or-offset detection at t+1 scored through a loose match. It is not a linking error a no-node relinker could find. A realistic version would steal a neighbour's continuation. That is free only when the neighbour is unannotated (127/129 here), which is the same "needs to know annotation" problem the conclusion uses to dismiss O_EDGEALL. Treat +0.006 of swap as a soft, partly unactionable ceiling, not as linking headroom.
3. APPLYING 1/6 TO AN ORACLE IS A CATEGORY ERROR. The line "perfect gated joint about +0.003 public" is also self-undermining: +0.003 would clear the +0.002 R4 bar. The 1/6 comes from three in-sample-tuned mechanisms, not from ceilings. The oracle has no public counterpart. What closes the line is realistic precision, not transfer.
4. THE BREAK-EVEN IS MISQUOTED. The conclusion quotes ~26.5% next to the realistic attach precisions (3.4%, 2.4%). 26.5% is the marginal break-even in the joint state, after oracle fork removal, where J=0.32 and D=99. On the base, where -0.0129 and -0.0273 were measured, it is ~0.16 for the first fork (division term only: gain 0.1/130 vs cost 0.1*J/131) and 0.114 averaged over the 200-FP volume (round 11). The verdict is unchanged, since 3.4% is far below either.
5. THE REQUIRED FRACTIONS ARE UNDERSTATED. The division term is convex: J=(25+x)/(130-y). Recovering a uniform fraction f of every oracle edit reaches +0.012 only at f=0.625 on the gated joint (not 58%) and f=0.339 on the wide joint (not 29%), with zero new errors.
6. SUPER-ADDITIVITY IS AN ORACLE-ONLY PROPERTY. The arithmetic and explanation are right: each attach TP is worth 1/99 instead of 1/130 once fork FPs are gone. Bootstrap excess +0.0015 [5-95% +0.0004, +0.0029]. But the same shrinking denominator makes every false fork more expensive: break-even precision rises from ~0.16 to ~0.20. Realistic mirror attach (7 TP / 200 FP) costs -0.0095 in the division term on the base but -0.0146 after fork removal. Realistic riders combine SUB-additively. "A bit more than their sum" must not be read as a case for bundling weak riders.
7. EMBRYO DOMINANCE. 6bba has 39/56 clips and 88/99 GT divisions; 44b6 has only 2/8/9 divisions. All 7 gated-attach TPs are in 6bba: O_ATT_g on 44b6 = 0, and there the full gated joint equals FP+LINK exactly (+0.02354). On 44b6 the joint is FP removal (+0.0070) plus swap-heavy linking (+0.0166). With the swap removed it is +0.0086. The test is two other embryos, so the division-side gain (+0.013 of the +0.021) rests on 7 and 31 events from one embryo. As a ceiling it is still robust: clip bootstrap gated joint +0.0206 [5-95% +0.0153, +0.0256]. An unpooled per-clip mean gives +0.0174.
Numbers verified as reported: base 0.93988 25/31/74; O_FP +0.00629; O_ATT_g +0.00541; O_LINK +0.00734; gated joint +0.02056; wide joint +0.04115; the 1/99-vs-1/130 excess +0.00169; 44b6/6bba splits; LINK decomposition.
corrected: Answer to the user, like for like: the three round-11 levers together (perfect fork removal + perfect gated orphan attach + perfect end->free-start linking with the 25 wrong-edge removals) measure +0.0143 lab. That is 44b6 +0.0086, 6bba +0.0146, singles sum 0.0128. Super-additive by +0.0015, all from the division denominator 130->99. So yes, above +0.01 as a ceiling, but only 1.19x the +0.012 bar, and below it on 44b6. The larger +0.0206 (gated) / +0.0412 (wide) adds a swap-relink oracle (+0.006). It is a missing/offset detection at t+1 matched loosely inside 7 um (GT move median 2.2 um, v-to-b 4.6 um, nearest other node to b 8.4 um), not fast motion. It is at best a soft ceiling. Reaching +0.012 needs a uniform 62.5% (gated) / 34% (wide) of every oracle edit with zero new errors. Realistic attach precision is 2-3% against a base break-even of 0.11-0.16. Realistic riders are sub-additive (the shrunken denominator makes false forks cost more), and no public transfer number applies to an oracle. Verdict unchanged: nothing is submittable before R8; finals stay #37 + #38.
